probes.note: insert at index 0: the C sets array->child to the new node and repairs the first element's prev, which is also the last-item cache
insert in the middle -- the plain relink, neither end of the list
index == size: get_array_item answers NULL, so this is already the APPEND path, not an in-place insert
an index far past the end does NOT fail. cJSON_InsertItemInArray falls through to add_item_to_array and appends (probed; spikes/place_relink.c)
insert into an empty array: the append path again, and the branch that starts a fresh list (item->prev = item)
which < 0 is the C's own guard -- false, document untouched, and the caller still owns the node it was handed
THE WITNESS: insert at the front rewrites the last-item cache, and only a later append reads it back (LESSONS #39). 99 must land at the END
same witness for the append path of insert
and for the fresh-list branch, where a wrong prev would make the next append the first element
an unresolvable selector: no target, so the op is a recorded no-op on both sides
a non-numeric index reads as 0 through the shared strtol rule before cJSON sees an int
20 digits overflow long; strtol saturates and the driver clamps to INT_MAX, which is then the append path
the selector reaches one level down, so insert runs on a nested array and the rest of the document must come back untouched
replace the first element, then append: the C has a special branch for parent->child == item and must still leave the cache right
replace in the middle
replace the LAST element -- the branch that writes parent->child->prev, i.e. the cache itself
the only element: the C's `parent->child->prev == parent->child` self-referential case
unlike insert, an out-of-range index IS a failure here: get_array_item answers NULL and ReplaceItemViaPointer rejects a NULL item
which < 0 guard
empty container: also the `parent->child == NULL` guard inside ReplaceItemViaPointer
replace inside a nested array
the replacement takes the SLOT, not the end: order is a,b,c afterwards

replace_item_in_object strdups the LOOKUP string into the replacement's key before looking anything up, so a case-INsensitive replace of `a` rewrites the member's spelling to `a`. Probed, because it is the opposite of what the name suggests
the case-SENSITIVE twin finds nothing, so the document is untouched
duplicate keys resolve to the first match, like every other object walk in the C

a missing key answers false. In the C the replacement has ALREADY been renamed at this point; the port consumes it by value, so there is no caller-visible node to have been mutated (DIVERGENCES.md, structural eliminations)
an array parent: get_object_item compares ->string, and array children have none, so false
empty object -- both the lookup and the child==NULL guard say no
a scalar parent: no child list to walk
an EMPTY key is a findable key, unlike the NULL key the C would create by inserting into an object -- which is exactly why `ins` refuses object targets
replace one level down
replace then detach the same key: the replacement must be findable under the key it was renamed to
five ops composing insert, replace, append and detach -- each step's descriptor is emitted, so a corruption at step 1 masked by step 4 is still visible
replace the last, then remove around it, appending after each -- the cache is read back three times
insert then immediately replace the node just inserted

probes.note: twelve op lines with a cap of eight: the last four are ignored so the descriptor stays bounded whatever the fuzzer sends
an unrecognized opcode records as `?` and changes nothing -- a fuzzed opcode cannot put arbitrary bytes into the descriptor
a document and no program at all: just the initial state
an unparseable document is rc 1 with nothing on stdout -- there is no tree to mutate
an interior NUL in the key: the C hands cJSON a C string, so the lookup is for `a` and the rename writes `a` -- everything after the NUL is invisible to it (LESSONS #29)
bytes 0x80-0xFF in a key: cJSON compares them verbatim with no UTF-8 validation, and so must the port
the C copies the op region into a NUL-terminated buffer and walks it with strchr, so everything past an interior NUL is invisible -- the second op never runs
